Aisha (Support): FYI escalated from Acme Mobile — customer says the SSE stream frequently cuts out mid-response when a user briefly hops between two Wi‑Fi APs (~500–1200ms blips). They get a truncated JSON chunk and client shows "stream ended". Can we triage?

Nora (Mobile PM): Thanks — which platforms/devices? iOS, Android? SDK version?

Aisha (Support): Android 12, our mobile SDK v1.8.2. Happens on their Pixel 5 and a range of cheap Androids. iOS report is much less frequent. They gave a sample session id and a small log: see below.

IncidentBot: New escalation created INC-1242 (priority: P2) :rotating_light:

Aisha (Support): log snippet from client (anonymized):
```
[INFO] start stream id=cli-93f4a token=tok-REDACTED
[data] received: {"id":"0","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"Hello"}}]}
[WARN] network flapped, transient: rssi=-84 -> -93
[ERROR] stream closed, reason=EOF, code=1006
[INFO] reconnect attempt 1 (delay 200ms)
[INFO] new conn id=cli-93f4b resume_token=rt-xyz
[data] received: {"id":"0","choices":[{"delta":{"content":" world"}}]}
[ERROR] parse error: unexpected EOF while reading JSON
```

Aisha (Support): Customer says they see two short connections back-to-back and then the final assembled payload is invalid JSON (partial chunk duplicated or truncated). Billing concern too — they got charged for two small sessions for one user action.

Liam (Eng SRE): Thanks — can you share the server trace ID for the original session? We need the inference-side logs to see whether we closed the generation, and whether resume requests were accepted or resulted in a fresh generation. Also want the edge/proxy logs around client IPs and TCP close types (RST vs FIN).

Aisha (Support): Provided trace_id=tr-8a7c3f. Edge logs from their tenant show: 
```
2026-03-11T14:20:12.123Z trace=tr-8a7c3f conn=7f9a CLOSE_REASON=keepalive-timeout
2026-03-11T14:20:12.125Z trace=tr-8a7c3f conn=7f9b NEW_CONN resume_token=rt-xyz client_ip=198.51.100.23
2026-03-11T14:20:12.450Z trace=tr-8a7c3f gen=gen-455 aborted_by=resume
```

Liam (Eng SRE): Interesting — looks like the server treats the resume as a fresh request that aborts the prior generation (aborted_by=resume). That creates a gap where the client may have received partial output from the first generation and then a different continuation from the resumed one. We should verify resume semantics in the SDK and whether we guarantee idempotent resume/appending.

Carlos (Platform Eng): On the runtime side, resume tokens currently map to session state but we have a <2s window where the old generation may still be streaming. If a resume arrives during that window we create a new generation and cancel the old to free GPU. That can cause partial duplicated fragments on the client if the client buffers and replays. Suggested fixes: 1) server-side: extend grace window to 1.5s and attempt to attach new connection to existing stream if possible; 2) client-side: increase reconnect backoff to >500ms and dedupe by sequence id; 3) billing: treat quick reconnects <2s as continuation credits (internal billing flag).

Nora (Mobile PM): For customer immediate mitigation, recommend they bump SDK reconnect delay to 600ms and enable client-side chunk dedupe (we can ship a small patch to the SDK). Can we ship a quick patched client lib?

Liam (Eng SRE): I can put a runtime guard in front of the generator: if resume_token == active and time_since_last_chunk < 1500ms, attach instead of spawn. Low-risk feature flag we can flip for this tenant. Carlos can you scope?

Carlos (Platform Eng): Yes I can implement feature-flagged attach behavior. Minimal changes to session manager. Will add telemetry: resumed_attach=true/false and attach_latency_ms. Estimated 2–3 engineer days.

Aisha (Support): Customer asked for repro steps we can tell them while we work on a fix. Proposed reproducible recipe we gave them:
```
1) Start stream from Android device with SDK v1.8.2, use a medium-length prompt (~150–300 tokens).
2) After first chunk is received, toggle Wi‑Fi off then on quickly (~600ms total). (adb shell svc wifi disable; sleep 0.6; svc wifi enable)
3) Let the client reconnect automatically (SDK default retry). Observe two connection ids and final assembled payload. Capture mobile logs and network capture (tcpdump) if possible.
4) Add header X-Debug-Resume: true to force resume token in server logs.
```

Nora (Mobile PM): We'll circulate this recipe to the customer and provide a patched SDK build that 1) delays reconnect to 600ms and 2) filters duplicate chunks by sequence id.

Aisha (Support): Customer also wants to know about billing credits for double-charged micro sessions. Can billing team mark quick double sessions (same resume token, gap <2s) as single billable unit?

Carlos (Platform Eng): I can emit an internal billing metric for resume_clustered=true and we can coordinate with billing to backfill/credit.

Liam (Eng SRE): Action items:
- Carlos: implement attach feature-flag + telemetry (2–3d)
- Mobile: ship SDK quick patch with 600ms backoff + chunk dedupe (this week)
- Support: share repro steps and request pcap + client logs from customer (Aisha)
- Billing: review billing-credit policy for clustered resumes (Carlos will prod Billing)

Aisha (Support): Thanks all. I'll send the repro steps and request pcap now. Customer is anxious so marking INC-1242 as P1 for human follow-up (we can keep technical P2). :eyes:
